column1: June 2004 saw the first passage, known as a ‘transit’, of the planet Venus across the face of the Sun in 122 years.
column2: 2004年6月，金星从日面前经过，这是122年来首次出现这种称为“凌日”的现象。

column1: Transits have helped shape our view of the whole Universe, as Heather Cooper and Nigel Henbest explain
column2: 正如希瑟·库珀和奈杰尔·亨贝斯特所解释的那样，凌日现象帮助我们形成了对整个宇宙的认识。

column1: On 8 June 2004, more than half the population of the world were treated to a rare astronomical event.
column2: 2004年6月8日，世界上超过一半的人有幸目睹了一次罕见的天象。

column1: For over six hours, the planet Venus steadily inched its way over the surface of the Sun.
column2: 在六个多小时里，金星一点一点地移过日面。
column5: inched its way|一点一点地移动

column1: This ‘transit’ of Venus was the first since 6 December 1882.
column2: 这是自1882年12月6日以来首次出现金星凌日。

column1: On that occasion, the American astronomer Professor Simon Newcomb led a party to South Africa to observe the event.
column2: 那一次，美国天文学家西蒙·纽康教授率领一队人前往南非观测这一天象。
column3: occasion|n. 特定的时候；那一次

column1: They were based at a girls’ school, where - it is alleged - the combined forces of three schoolmistresses outperformed the professionals with the accuracy of their observations.
column2: 他们以一所女子学校为驻地，据说，那里的三位女教师通力合作，观测结果比专业人士的还要准确。

column1: For centuries, transits of Venus have drawn explorers and astronomers alike to the four corners of the globe.
column2: 几个世纪以来，金星凌日吸引着探险家和天文学家奔赴世界各地。
column8: the four corners of the globe|世界各地

column1: And you can put it all down to the extraordinary polymath Edmond Halley.
column2: 而这一切都可归功于非凡的博学之士埃德蒙·哈雷。
column3: put it all down to|把……归因于

column1: In November 1677, Halley observed a transit of the innermost planet, Mercury, from the desolate island of St Helena in the South Pacific.
column2: 1677年11月，哈雷在南太平洋荒凉的圣赫勒拿岛上观测到了水星凌日。水星是离太阳最近的行星。

column1: He realised that, from different latitudes, the passage of the planet across the Sun’s disc would appear to differ.
column2: 他意识到，从不同纬度观察，行星在日面上经过的路径看起来会有所不同。

column1: By timing the transit from two widely-separated locations, teams of astronomers could calculate the parallax angle - the apparent difference in position of an astronomical body due to a difference in the observer’s position.
column2: 天文学家们可以在两个相距很远的地点分别为凌日计时，据此算出视差角，也就是因观测者位置不同而造成的天体视位置之差。

column1: Calculating this angle would allow astronomers to measure what was then the ultimate goal: the distance of the Earth from the Sun.
column2: 算出这个角度，天文学家就能测出他们当时最想知道的距离，也就是地球与太阳之间的距离。

column1: This distance is known as the ‘astronomical unit’ or AU.
column2: 这个距离称为“天文单位”，简称AU。

column1: Halley was aware that the AU was one of the most fundamental of all astronomical measurements.
column2: 哈雷知道，天文单位是所有天文测量值中最基本的指标之一。

column1: Johannes Kepler, in the early 17th century, had shown that the distances of the planets from the Sun governed their orbital speeds, which were easily measurable.
column2: 早在17世纪初，约翰内斯·开普勒就已证明，行星与太阳之间的距离决定了它们的公转速度，而公转速度很容易测量。

column1: But no-one had found a way to calculate accurate distances to the planets from the Earth.
column2: 但当时还没有人找到准确计算地球到各行星距离的方法。

column1: The goal was to measure the AU; then, knowing the orbital speeds of all the other planets round the Sun, the scale of the Solar System would fall into place.
column2: 目标是测出一个天文单位有多长。有了这个距离，再知道其他各行星绕太阳运行的速度，太阳系的尺度便可随之确定。

column1: However, Halley realised that Mercury was so far away that its parallax angle would be very difficult to determine.
column2: 然而，哈雷意识到，水星距离地球很远，要测定它的视差角会非常困难。

column1: As Venus was closer to the Earth, its parallax angle would be larger, and Halley worked out that by using Venus it would be possible to measure the Sun’s distance to 1 part in 500.
column2: 由于金星离地球更近，它的视差角会更大。哈雷算出，借助金星来测量日地距离，精度有望达到五百分之一。

column1: But there was a problem: transits of Venus, unlike those of Mercury, are rare, occurring in pairs roughly eight years apart every hundred or so years.
column2: 但有一个困难。与水星凌日不同，金星凌日很少发生，大约每隔一百年才成对出现，同一对的两次凌日相隔约八年。

column1: Nevertheless, he accurately predicted that Venus would cross the face of the Sun in both 1761 and 1769 - though he didn’t survive to see either.
column2: 尽管如此，他还是准确预言金星会在1761年和1769年两度掠过日面，只是他没能活到亲眼见证其中任何一次。
column8: either|pron. 两者中的任何一次

column1: Inspired by Halley’s suggestion of a way to pin down the scale of the Solar System, teams of British and French astronomers set out on expeditions to places as diverse as India and Siberia.
column2: 哈雷提出了一种确定太阳系尺度的方法。受此启发，英法两国的天文学家组队远行，前往印度、西伯利亚等迥然不同的地方考察。

column1: But things weren’t helped by Britain and France being at war.
column2: 但英法两国当时正在交战，这使事情更不顺利。

column1: The person who deserves most sympathy is the French astronomer Guillaume Le Gentil.
column2: 最值得同情的是法国天文学家纪尧姆·勒让蒂。

column1: He was thwarted by the fact that the British were besieging his observation site at Pondicherry in India.
column2: 由于英军当时正在围困他位于印度本地治里的观测点，他的计划受了阻。

column1: Fleeing on a French warship crossing the Indian Ocean, Le Gentil saw a wonderful transit - but the ship’s pitching and rolling ruled out any attempt at making accurate observations.
column2: 勒让蒂搭上一艘横渡印度洋的法国军舰撤离，在船上目睹了一次壮观的金星凌日。但船身前后颠簸、左右摇晃，他根本无法进行准确观测。

column1: Undaunted, he remained south of the equator, keeping himself busy by studying the islands of Mauritius and Madagascar before setting off to observe the next transit in the Philippines.
column2: 他没有气馁，继续留在赤道以南。他先忙于考察毛里求斯岛和马达加斯加岛，随后动身前往菲律宾，准备观测下一次凌日。

column1: Ironically after travelling nearly 50,000 kilometres, his view was clouded out at the last moment, a very dispiriting experience.
column2: 颇具讽刺意味的是，他奔波了近五万公里，最后关头却被云层挡住了视线，实在令人沮丧。
column6: at the last moment|在最后关头

column1: While the early transit timings were as precise as instruments would allow, the measurements were dogged by the ‘black drop’ effect.
column2: 早期的凌日计时已经达到了当时仪器所能达到的精度，测量结果却一直受到“黑滴效应”的干扰。

column1: When Venus begins to cross the Sun’s disc, it looks smeared not circular - which makes it difficult to establish timings.
column2: 金星开始掠过日面时，看上去轮廓模糊，不呈圆形，因此很难准确判定时间。

column1: This is due to diffraction of light.
column2: 这是光的衍射造成的。

column1: The second problem is that Venus exhibits a halo of light when it is seen just outside the Sun’s disc.
column2: 第二个问题是，当人们看到金星刚好位于日面以外时，它的周围会出现一圈光晕。

column1: While this showed astronomers that Venus was surrounded by a thick layer of gases refracting sunlight around it, both effects made it impossible to obtain accurate timings.
column2: 这固然让天文学家看出，金星周围包裹着一层厚厚的气体，这些气体使阳光在金星周围发生折射，但这两种效应使人无法准确计时。
column9: accurate timings|n. 准确的计时结果

column1: But astronomers laboured hard to analyse the results of these expeditions to observe Venus transits.
column2: 尽管如此，天文学家仍投入了大量精力，分析这些远征观测金星凌日所得的结果。

column1: Johann Franz Encke, Director of the Berlin Observatory, finally determined a value for the AU based on all these parallax measurements: 153,340,000 km.
column2: 柏林天文台台长约翰·弗朗茨·恩克综合所有这些视差测量结果，终于算出一个天文单位的长度为153,340,000公里。

column1: Reasonably accurate for the time, that is quite close to today’s value of 149,597,870 km, determined by radar, which has now superseded transits and all other methods in accuracy.
column2: 以当时的条件衡量，这个数值相当准确，与如今用雷达测得的149,597,870公里非常接近。就精度而言，雷达测量如今已胜过凌日观测和其他所有方法。
column5: for the time|以当时的条件衡量

column1: The AU is a cosmic measuring rod, and the basis of how we scale the Universe today.
column2: 天文单位就像一把宇宙量尺，是我们今天衡量宇宙尺度的基础。

column1: The parallax principle can be extended to measure the distances to the stars.
column2: 视差原理还可以推广，用于测量恒星与我们的距离。

column1: If we look at a star in January - when Earth is at one point in its orbit - it will seem to be in a different position from where it appears six months later.
column2: 假设我们在一月观测一颗恒星，此时地球位于其公转轨道上的某一点，那么这颗恒星看上去的位置会与六个月后看到的不同。

column1: Knowing the width of Earth’s orbit, the parallax shift lets astronomers calculate the distance.
column2: 知道了地球轨道的宽度，天文学家就可以利用视差所造成的视位置偏移算出恒星的距离。

column1: June 2004’s transit of Venus was thus more of an astronomical spectacle than a scientifically important event.
column2: 所以，2004年6月的金星凌日更像是一场天文奇观，其科学意义相对有限。

column1: But such transits have paved the way for what might prove to be one of the most vital breakthroughs in the cosmos - detecting Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars.
column2: 不过，历次凌日观测为一项可能跻身宇宙探索最重大突破之列的发现铺平了道路，那就是探测绕其他恒星运行、大小与地球相当的行星。
column3: paved the way for|为……铺平道路
column9: Earth-sized|adj. 与地球大小相当的
